messages:
Ivy K: Quick heads-up: I spotted a couple of structured-output examples that break after the recent invoke API rename. The sample JSON schema still expects the old tool output shape (flat object) but a few examples now return an envelope.

Devon R: Can you paste an example line? I want to see whether it's the docs sample or the sample app.

Ivy K: Sure: the structured-output page has `expected: { type: 'object', properties: { answer: { type: 'string' } }, additionalProperties: false }` but the example LLM output shows `{ "result": { "answer": "..." } }`. Parser snippets in docs assume raw object; will fail strict validators.

Sophie L: Thanks. Two immediate options: 1) update the examples to the new envelope shape everywhere, 2) show both patterns (raw / enveloped) + add parsing hint. I prefer option 2 for a transitional period.

Alex M: Agree with Sophie. Also propose a tiny compatibility helper in the SDK docs: `const unbox = (v) => v?.result ?? v` — include as a recommended snippet under the parsing patterns section. Mark it as temporary.

Ivy K: Love that. Can we also add a short migration checklist in the invoke guide: find uses of `tools.call` and `tools.invoke` (old names), replace with `call({toolName, input})`, and opt into the envelope or use unbox?

Devon R: I'll draft the checklist. Also will run the docs link-checker; there are a bunch of sample app links that point at the branch name that was deleted. I'll fix URLs to use the canonical example-invoke-app main branch.

Sophie L: Small extra: for the JSON Schema examples, add a small note showing how to allow the envelope without weakening validation: show both schemas and a short TypeScript parse helper: ```ts
function parseCandidate(candidate: any) {
  const raw = candidate?.result ?? candidate;
  // validate raw against schema here
  return raw;
}
```
This keeps `additionalProperties: false` in place.

Alex M: Will include that snippet. Also planning to open a single PR with: link fixes, schema dual-examples, SDK parsing helper snippet, and a short compat shim example. PR body will reference this thread and link to the issue for removing the shim later.

redwood-docs-bot: PR creation detected: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1501 (draft) audit-trail:files changed: 5 :memo:

Devon R: I added a quick test in docs/examples/harness that loads example responses and asserts `parseCandidate(example)` returns an object matching the schema. If the harness sees an envelope it unboxes and validates. That should catch regressions.

Ivy K: Nice. Can we also add a small note in the CHANGELOG under docs: "Invoke API example path changes and temporary parsing helper added" so folks using our snippets know why.

Alex M: Done in the PR draft. Also left a TODO comment in the compat snippet: "// TODO: remove after all docs snippets migrated (tracking: #1520)".

redwood-docs-bot: CI queued for PR #1501: link-check, lint, examples-harness. Status: running :gear:

Sophie L: One nit from me on wording: avoid the phrase "tools.call is deprecated" in user-facing guides; prefer "previous helper names" and link to migration. Keeps tone less scary.

Devon R: Good call. Updated PR text accordingly.

redwood-docs-bot: CI result for PR #1501: link-check passed, lint passed, examples-harness passed. Merging in 10s. :tada:

Alex M: PR merged to main -> docs. I'll follow up with a short internal note in #eng-devex outlining when we plan to remove the compat shim (tentative: two weeks).

Ivy K: Thanks everyone. I'll create tracking issue #1520 for the final sweep and assign owners for the remaining example apps that need one-off fixes.

Sophie L: Great closure. Add a line in the invoke guide top-level note: "If you rely on our snippets, we recommend running the example harness locally (yarn docs:test-examples) to surface link/schema mismatches."

Alex M: Added that. Thread resolved.
